_Despierta a tus sueños_

_Bodhi_ es la definición de sustentabilidad en bienes raíces: con técnicas de construcción de bajo impacto para el suelo y un concepto enfocado en integrarse en armonía con la naturaleza, Bodhi es la mejor representación del espíritu selvático que desean los que harán de Tulum su hogar.  

🌱 Baja densidad: sólo 41 unidades en 10,000 m2 de terreno                                     
🌱 70 por ciento de áreas verdes preservadas                           
🌱 Cimentación sobre pilotes: para minimizar el impacto en la permeabilidad del suelo sin remover vegetación y dejando espacio para la fauna local.
🌱 Diseño bioclimático: Aprovechamos las condiciones naturales para optimizar la iluminación y la ventilación en cada una de las 11 torres. 
🌱 Tecnología ecológica: captación de agua de lluvias, paneles solares, planta de tratamiento de agua, tratamiento de residuos orgánicos, vidrios aislantes de doble panel y albercas con filtración biológica.

22/05/25 7:45 a. m. - +52 984 463 9350: 🔴THE HOTTEST DAYS OF 2025 WILL ARRIVE IN MEXICO.

The DOG HEATS season, the 40 hottest days of the year, begins on July 3rd, and 2025 could break all historical temperature records.
Heat waves exceeding 45°C are expected in several areas of Mexico.

And although it sometimes goes unnoticed, the dog heats are one of the most dangerous times of the year, especially for children, the elderly, and pets.

📢 Here's how to prepare:

🐶 DOGS
1. Don't take them for walks between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m. The asphalt can reach 65°C and burn their paws in seconds.
2. Always leave them fresh water in the shade. Heatstroke can kill them in less than 15 minutes.
 3. Never leave them locked in the car. Even for a short time, temperatures can exceed 70°C in minutes.

👶 CHILDREN
1. Keep them from playing in direct sunlight. Their skin is thinner and they dehydrate much more quickly.
2. Dress them in lightweight, cotton, and light-colored clothing.
3. Offer them water constantly, even if they are not thirsty. Thirst is a late sign of dehydration.

👵 ELDERLY PEOPLE
1. Many older adults lose their sense of thirst. Offer them water frequently.
2. Keep them from going out during the hottest hours. Their thermal regulation system no longer responds as well.
3. Check their blood pressure, breathing, and mood. Heat can cause confusion, dizziness, or fainting.

30/08/25 6:15 p. m. - +52 984 463 9350: Here’s how the new registry, licensing, and municipal decision-making in Quintana Roo will affect expat owners—non-residents owning and renting out properties on platforms like Airbnb:

1. Mandatory Registration (RETUR-Q)

All hosts—including non-residents—must register with the State Tourism Registry (RETUR‑Q) to legally operate short‑term rentals. Registration must be updated annually. Non-compliance can lead to sanctions. 

2. State Operating License via SATQ

Hosts must obtain a state operating license from the Tax Administration Service of Quintana Roo (SATQ). This involves an in‑person appointment and submitting documentation like:

Proof of property ownership

Cadastral code

Tax status certificate

Title deed

Property registry number (ballot)

INE or legal representative ID 


3. Lodging Tax (ISH)

A 6% lodging tax (Impuesto Sobre Hospedaje) is now applied to short‑term rentals in Quintana Roo. This tax must be collected from guests and remitted to the state, typically facilitated by platforms like Airbnb. 

4. Digital Platform Tax Obligations

Digital platforms are required to withhold and remit:

VAT (IVA) — 16% of rental charges, remitted to the federal government 

Income Tax (ISR) —

4% withholding if you have a Mexican Tax ID (RFC)

20% withholding if you do not have an RFC 



To minimize withholding, expats should obtain a Mexican RFC, even if non-residents.

5. Enforcement & Compliance

Beginning January 1, 2024, authorities began cross-checking hosts listed on digital platforms against the SATQ database. Non-compliant hosts (i.e. unregistered, lacking licenses, or not paying taxes) face restrictions, fines, or operational shutdowns.  Authorities may also verify host contact information and inspect properties. 


---

Summary Table: What Expats Must Do

Requirement	Action for Expat Hosts

RETUR‑Q Registration	Register annually with State Tourism Registry
**Operating License (SATQ)**	Schedule visit, submit required documentation, renew annually
**Lodging Tax (ISH)**	Collect 6% from guests, remit via platform or directly to state authorities
VAT (IVA)	16% collected by platform, remitted to federal government
**Income Tax Withholding (ISR)**	Obtain RFC to reduce withholding to 4% (vs. 20% without RFC)
Enforcement Risks	Non-compliance may lead to fines, shutdown, or platform listing removal

Better to be safe than sorry!
